name: ASCII CRT
summary: Everything is a real glyph on a monospace grid, lit by the amber phosphor of an old monochrome tube: typed titles, inverse-video tags, ASCII pictures built from a density ramp, banner numerals, a LOG strip for captions, one soft blue switched on once, scanlines and bloom.

palette.use: the unlit glass: warm near-black, the ground of every frame
phosphor at normal brightness (0.7): every glyph's middle tone
phosphor dim (0.42): timestamps, separators, far planes, the low end of the ramp
barely lit cells and the dashed LOG separator's gaps (proposed: the dim end of the ramp at 15%)
phosphor overexposed (1.0): bold glyphs, the cursor, landing flashes
the one soft second colour, for the one thing only: blue light. Switched on once, never decoration

type.emphasis: brightness (dim 0.42 / normal 0.7 / bold 1.0), inverse video, a bigger grid, slower typing

banned: an image or a photo run through an "ASCII filter": every character is drawn as a character on the grid
falling green code rain, hacker-movie clichés
pixel-art sprites, free pixels, vector lines or floating HUD panels
a second hue for decoration: the one second colour belongs to one thing, switched on once
an RGB grille (a monochrome tube has none)
crossfades between screens: clear, redraw, scroll, power on/off
copying any film's or product's interface text, fonts or logos; real agency names
